Row.StatusText: **Position 6 of nine** — ratified 2026-09-04 at position 3, renumbered 2026-09-05 by [D28](#d28), [D29](#d29) and [D31](#d31); earlier still, "after position 3". Row.name: C-CONSTRAINT-DURABILITY
Row.Charter: A rule in `skills/ngrace/ngrace-spec/SKILL.md` and its packaged mirror: `Constraints` holds durable scope facts; authoring-pass sequencing (*"spec only in this pass"*, *"status remains draft"*, *"do not author plan.xml until approved"*) belongs to the brief and the gate, never to the artifact that outlives the pass. Searched before minting: `C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT` governs the executor's contract, `C-APPROVAL-SCOPE` the phrase and close acts, `C-PLAN-QUALITY` plan-side richness; none says what `Constraints` may contain.

Row.name: C-APPROVE-TARGET-DISCOVERY
Row.Charter: A bare `ngrace gate approve` targets whatever **lacks an attestation** rather than falling through to `plan`. The fallthrough is `src/gates/ledger.ts:1505-1514` (cited as `:1256-1267` in [F129.1](#f129.1), before the file moved), so on a bundle whose spec and plan are both `approved` a bare approve re-stamps `plan`, reports success, and a user who does not know `--artifact` can never attest the spec. Named here 2026-09-04; F129.1 asked for the slot and minted no name. Searched before minting: `C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT` made the gate the status writer, `C-APPROVAL-SCOPE` owns the phrase and the close acts, `C-APPROVE-TIME-REVIEW` owns *when review runs*; none changes what a bare approve targets.

Row.name: C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE
Row.Charter: Convert this repository's 65/65 module-markup baseline from a hand-maintained convention into a gate: a lint rule (`require-module-contract`, id namespaced to the catalog's `markup.*` family) whose predicate is that every `src/**/*.ts` outside `.test.ts`, fixtures and explicitly ignored shims begins with a valid `START_MODULE_CONTRACT` header. Closes the conditional-validator hole in [F162](#f162) — `markup.unknown-link` validates a `LINKS:` that already exists and `graph.module-without-linked-files` fires graph-to-file, so a new source file carrying no markup silently leaves the governed set while the repository stays green. **Zero remediation diff today**: the tree already satisfies the predicate, and the rule locks the baseline permanently. Named here 2026-09-05 by [D29](#d29). Searched before minting: `C-GRAPH-COVERAGE` covered graph module/Path coverage from the graph side, `C-ADOPTION-SURFACE` the lifecycle doc surface, `C-ABSENCE-VALUE` recorded the `START_MODULE_CONTRACT` NonGoal this overturns in part, and `C-CONTRACT-DEBT` / `C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT` are API-error and execution-protocol contracts; none gates markup presence.
Row.StatusText: **Position 4 of nine** — ratified 2026-09-05 at position 3, renumbered by [D31](#d31). Narrow leaf-level verification fix, and it ships before any function contract is written.

Row.name: C-FUNCTION-CONTRACT-SURFACE
Row.Charter: Adopt `START_CONTRACT:` on this repository's governed surface — declarations exported from the command surface and public engine facade, plus every function that writes, transitions or validates audit state, ledger records or git operations — excluding internal leaf helpers, utility transformers and purely file-scoped helpers. Block markers stay reserved for complex control flow (multi-step validations, rollback ladders, transaction scopes) and are disallowed in flat sequential logic. **The validator rule ships simultaneously with the initial target annotations**, never annotations first and enforcement later ([D28](#d28), [D29](#d29)). The command surface is `src/grace.ts`, eleven `src/grace-*.ts` modules and `src/gates/command.ts`, `src/review/command.ts`, `src/query/command.ts` — the directory `src/commands/` **does not exist** and the ruling's path is corrected in [F162](#f162). Named here 2026-09-05 by [D29](#d29). Searched before minting: as for `C-MODULE-CONTRACT-GATE`, plus `C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE`, which covers explainer coverage rather than source annotation.
Row.StatusText: **Position 9 of nine** — ratified 2026-09-05 at position 8, renumbered by [D31](#d31). Downstream of the gate. The load-bearing subset is the spec's to define and defend; roughly 433 exported declarations exist across the 65 files and the in-scope subset is much smaller — measure it, never assume it.

Row.name: C-ROADMAP-XML
Row.Charter: **Name.** `C-ROADMAP-XML`. **Searched before minting**, 2026-09-06 at `408f2ae`, over `.ngrace/changes/archive/` and the whole record for any `C-*` containing `ROADMAP`, `XML`, `PLANS`, `CONVERT`, `MARKDOWN` or `DOC`: **zero hits**. No prior name covers this ground. **Charter.** Convert the remaining governed markdown under `docs/plans/` to XML, once `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` has moved the record. Ships with the check that makes it safe. **Scope, measured 2026-09-06 at `408f2ae` — 15 files.** Rule: `find docs/plans/active -name '*.md'` excluding `decisions.md`, plus the index. | group | count | files | |---|---|---| | roadmap `review.md` | 6 | `RM-DESIGN-EVIDENCE`, `RM-GITLESS-INTEGRITY`, `RM-GOVERNED-PATH`, `RM-LANGUAGE-EXTENSIBILITY`, `RM-PILOT-APPROVAL`, `RM-VERIFIED-APPROVAL` | | roadmap `plan.md` | 1 | `RM-GOVERNED-PATH` | | `p0-*` derivations | 4 | under `RM-GOVERNED-PATH` | | `brownfield-*` findings | 2 | under `RM-GOVERNED-PATH` | | merged source | 1 | `sources/RM-GOVERNED-PATH-merged.md` | | plan index | 1 | `docs/plans/README.md` | **Permanently out of scope, and why — these are not omissions.** - `docs/plans/archive/` — **13** markdown files, immutable ([CLAUDE.md](../../../../CLAUDE.md)). The repository stays mixed-format there **forever**; "no markdown at all" is unreachable for archives and the charter must say so rather than imply otherwise. - `skills/ngrace/*/SKILL.md` and the packaged mirror — **16 + 16** files. `SKILL.md` is an external format contract of the Claude skill/plugin packaging, not a house choice. - `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` — the harness instruction file and the marketplace-facing overview, both fixed filenames read by other systems. `CLAUDE.md:22` documents the roadmap layout and must be **updated**, not converted. - `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md` — owned by `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2`. **Enforcement ships with the structure, never after it** ([D28](#d28)). [F177](#f177)'s dangling-citation check is this bundle's **first** deliverable, not a follow-on: a validator that resolves outbound `docs/plans/**` paths written inside archived artifacts and reports the ones that no longer exist. Without it the conversion repeats, at 15 files, the silent breakage that already left **15** archived bundles citing a `plan.md` path that does not exist. **Why the position matters, measured.** **40 of 68** archived bundles cite some `docs/plans/active/<RM>/` path (rule: `grep -rl` over archived `spec.xml` and `plan.xml`, counted by bundle directory). Exposure to silent citation decay therefore accrues with nearly every bundle that archives, which is an argument for scheduling the check early rather than at the tail. **Position 4**, ratified 2026-09-06 by the maintainer. The insertion and the six positions it shifts are recorded in [D32](#d32); read the order from there, never from [D31](#d31), which this amends.

Row.name: C-CODIFY-DECISIONS
Row.Charter: **Chartered 2026-09-07 by the maintainer**, verbatim: *"option C"*, on four itemized variants. The position is deferred **deliberately, and the deferral is the point**: a position decision costs the decisions genre roughly forty lines, and that genre is already forty lines over its window, while a charter row costs it nothing — staged charter rows are not `[FD]\d` entries and so are not counted in the decisions wrap at all. Ratify a position once this bundle has made room. Priority needs no stating in the meantime: this is the only chartered work that can open the rulings window, so nothing else can sensibly precede it. **Charter.** Give the decisions genre a working retirement trigger. **It is not, as this row first read, the thing blocking the flush** — that claim was a measurement artifact, corrected the same day in [F191](#f191): both genres fit their windows today. What remains true is that **no live decision carries a resolving `CodifiedIn` or `TaughtIn`** — 59 live, zero tagged, against a retired sibling holding exactly one ([D24](#d24)). The precedent is a sample of one, so the genre can still only grow, and the ceiling will bind eventually rather than now. - **Codification alone may not be enough, and the spec must prove which.** [`C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW`](#named-bundle-registry) applied its window formula to the **findings genre only**; the rulings call site still clamps against the post-move base. Whether a decisions-genre retirement opens the window, leaves it unchanged, or shrinks it is a question to derive from the code and confirm on a fixture — not to assume from the findings behaviour. - **The evidence standard is the load-bearing question.** [D28.1](#d28.1) retires a decision when its prose invariant is *permanently replaced by an automated machine check* that enforces it *unconditionally*. A tag on a decision merely **related** to a shipped test retires live governance text on a false premise, and retirement is one-way in practice. [D24](#d24)'s tag was gated on two **named tests passing at execution**, which is the pattern. - **`TaughtIn` versus `CodifiedIn` is unresolved.** Teaching a rule in skill prose is not enforcement, so a spec that uses the tag without settling what it means is deciding by accident. - **The bundle must pay for itself.** Whatever chartering and closing costs the decisions genre, the scope must retire more, with margin — every staged figure on this work has aged in the same direction.
